title: 1:1 prep — Samir Patel (weekly) — Mar 16 2026 — scratchpad
linked_artifacts: JIRA: INF-118 (infra: OOM on NVLink host)

content:
Purpose: quick prep notes before my weekly 1:1 with Samir (aim 30m). Keep it compact; prioritize blockers, decisions, and career check-in. Goal: leave with 3 clear action items and alignment on next delivery date for the KV cache work.

Meeting logistics
- When: Tue 2026-03-16, 10:00am PT
- Duration: 30 minutes
- Mode: video (default) — flag if Samir wants async update instead
- Note: He asked for a short deep-dive on batching heuristics last week; reserve 8–10 mins for that.

Agenda (tentative order)
1) Quick personal pulse (2–3m) — energy, bandwidth, headcount stressors
2) Blockers & escalation (8–10m) — INF-118 impact, PR 4321 readiness, perf regression risk
3) Technical deep-dive (8–10m) — batching / KV cache knob choices and rollout plan
4) Career / growth (5m) — promotion timeline prep + mentoring ask follow-up
5) Action items & sync points (2m)

Notes to self: start by asking how he slept on the weekend — small empathy wins. If he seems tapped out, offer to shift priorities or take ownership of a downstream ask (e.g., customer demo stabilization).

Blockers & context (to raise)
- INF-118 (JIRA): we've seen OOMs on NVLink hosts when kv-cache entries hit ~12GB under long-context tests. Samir's patch reduced memory churn but not peak resident. Need clear rollout plan and fallback policy.
  - Ask: Do you have a safe canary config we can use that caps sequence length and disables large-prefix caching?
  - Risk: If we roll current patch to Dedicated pools, SLA customers might see latency spikes. Put a rollback window.

- PR 4321: batching improvements — currently blocked by infra test flakes (flaky CI on aarch64 instance). Samir mentioned an infra ticket to repro; check status.
  - Ask: can we spin a reproducible job on a stable a100 staging node? If not, I should escalate to infra SRE (cc: Priya).

- Customer impact: demo for Acme scheduled 2026-03-23; must ensure KV cache stable for long-context generator. If not, propose plan B: revert to smaller context + synthetic prompt rewrite for the demo.

Deep-dive topic: batching heuristics & KV cache knobs (points to hit)- Summary of current approach: adaptive minibatching with sequence bucketing by length + timeouts = good P99 but can starve small requests under load.
- Two knobs under consideration: increase max_batch_latency to 20ms vs reduce max_batch_size from 64->48. Need tradeoffs: latency vs throughput, cost per token.
- Question to Samir: Which metric should we prioritize for Dedicated tier customers by default? My bias: preserve P99 latency for PLG tiers, optimize throughput for Dedicated contracted pools (they expect throughput/price guarantees).
- Simple experiment: run A/B traffic (10k tokens) with knob set A/B for 24hrs across two identical pools. Can we schedule this with the CI job?

Career & coaching items
- Samir is on the promotion track (senior -> staff) — last calibration email was positive but asked for more cross-team influence examples.
  - Remind him to add 1–2 short bullet examples to his promotion doc: a) led the KV cache design; b) preempted priority inversion in batching pipeline; c) mentored two ICs to ship PRs.
  - Offer: I will draft a short endorsement paragraph once he sends the bullets. Deadline: EOD Thu 2026-03-19.
- Mentoring ask: He wanted help with stakeholder calls (Solutions eng). Offer to join first call as co-owner or do a prep/role-play. Suggest we schedule a 30m prep in next week.

Feedback to deliver (gentle + specific)
- Positive: Great ownership on the KV cache prototype and clear design docs — call that out.
- Area to improve: include more explicit rollback criteria in PR descriptions (e.g., memory/latency thresholds + validation plan). Give a concrete phrasing he can copy into PR template.

Decisions I want by EOD Wed 2026-03-17
- Confirm canary config (yes/no) for rolling INF-118 fix to dedicated pools
- Confirm experiment A/B schedule for batching knobs (who will run it?)

Draft follow-ups to produce after meeting (todo for me)
- Quick TL;DR email to Samir summarizing action items and owners (send within 1 hour after 1:1)
- If he agrees to canary, create rollout ticket and assign to SRE with rollback window and monitoring checklist (include metrics: resident mem, p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate).
- Add a promotion bullets PR to his profile and draft endorsement paragraph.

Action items (clear, owner, due)
- Samir: Add 2 cross-team impact bullets to promotion doc (due 2026-03-18)
- Me (Elena): Draft endorsement paragraph after he adds bullets (due 2026-03-19)
- Samir + infra: Reproduce PR 4321 flaky test on stable a100 (target 2026-03-19)
- Me: If canary approved, create rollout ticket + assign to Priya (SRE) and add monitoring checklist (due 2026-03-17)
- Samir: Prepare short slide for Acme demo plan B (reduce context framing) if KV cache not stabilized (due 2026-03-20)

Reminders & loose ideas (notes to self)
- Consider offering Samir a small shadowing slot on my stakeholder sync with Sales next Tue to increase exposure.
- Track his time balance — two 2-week sprints of deep debugging may cause burnout. Suggest 2 half-days/week of no-meetings for focus work if needed.
- Link the KV cache metric dashboard to his PR description (reduces friction for reviewers).

End-of-meeting script (closing lines to use)
- "Thanks — that was helpful. I'll send a short note with the 3 actions and we can reconfirm on Thursday if anything shifts."
- If he seems overloaded: "Let's offload one item to me or pause the non-critical experiment this sprint."

Post-meeting send (subject): 1:1 recap — Samir (Mar 16) — action items- Body: 3 bullets: (1) promotion bullets due 3/18 (Samir), (2) canary decision by Wed 3/17 (Samir + Elena/SRE), (3) I'll create rollout ticket if green. Attach links to PR 4321 and INF-118.

Bottom-line priority: unblock PR 4321 repro + decide safe canary window for INF-118. If both green, we can keep Acme demo plan A. Otherwise prepare plan B.

Scratch: potential wording for promotion endorsement (draft to edit after meeting):"Samir consistently drives complex cross-cutting initiatives in the serving runtime: he designed and implemented the KV cache prototype, led the batching performance work, and mentor peers on production-grade testing practices. He effectively balances short-term incident responses with longer-term performance investments, making him ready for a Staff-level scope."

(leave room below for live notes during 1:1)
